connectionsIntro: Link Discord and Telegram so bridge bots can map those accounts to this AgentLayer user (same tenant_id as in Admin → Users). Tool credentials are stored per service_key (encrypted on the server). Known tools can ship a small form schema in the tool module (TOOL_USER_SECRET_FORMS) so this page shows the right fields — e.g. Gmail wants your address plus a Google App Password, not your normal login password. Keys like weather or time are names chosen by the tool author for a secret slot (often an API key or URL you paste once). Not saved means you have not stored anything for that key yet — not that the key name is invalid.
connectionsDiscordIntro: Paste your numeric Discord user id (Developer Mode → right‑click your profile → Copy User ID). The Discord gateway runs inside agent-layer when an admin enables it under Admin → Interfaces. This field only links your Discord account to your AgentLayer user; it does not replace normal login.
connectionsTelegramIntro: Telegram does not show your numeric user id under Settings / profile — you need a bot for that. Open a chat with @getidsbot, tap Start or send /start; the reply lists your user id (digits only). Copy that number here. If @getidsbot does not answer, try another id bot (e.g. @RawDataBot). The Telegram gateway runs inside agent-layer when an admin enables it under Admin → Interfaces. In groups, disable bot privacy via @BotFather /setprivacy so the bot can see normal messages (same idea as Discord channels). This field only links your Telegram account; it does not replace normal login.
